section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1971
title: 8 The variations in the incidence of Accidental deaths in different regions resulted from a large number of factors peculiar to the region, such as topography of the area, population, level of industrialisation and other socio-economic factors. Considering population as one of the major concomitant variants, the volume of accidental deaths per one lakh of population in different States and Union Territories and Cities has been estimated and is presented in Table 4. The highest number of accidental deaths occurred in the State of Maharashtra (20,318) followed by Uttar Pradesh (14,542) and Madhya Pradesh (11,698). These three States together accounted for more than 45% of the total accidental deaths in the entire country. The volume of accidental deaths per one lakh of population was the highest in Maharashtra (40.2) followed by Madhya Pradesh (27.9) as against the All India average of (19.2). In all other States it was round about 20 or less. In Nagaland it was only 1.9. Among the Union Territories the highest volume per one lakh of population was in the Andaman & Nicobar Islands 51.7, while it was only 3.1 in Lakshadweep. Among the Cities under study, the volume of accidental deaths was the highest in Bombay 63.6 while in all other Cities it was far less than in Bombay, the average for all the Cities together being 36.9.
